newsitem.title: USA: H.J. Heinz sees double-digit growth in 1998.
newsitem.headline: H.J. Heinz sees double-digit growth in 1998.

text.p: H. J. Heinz Co, which reported earnings of $1.93 a share excluding one-time items for the fiscal year ended April 30, 1997, up 10.3 percent from the year before, said on Tuesday that it expects to deliver a double-digit earnings increase in fiscal 1998.

The Pittsburgh-based ketchup maker and owner of Weight Watchers said that it expects its restructuring to yield significant returns for shareholders and enhance the company's ability to deliver continued double-digit earnings growth into the next century.
Net sales, which increased 2.7 percent in fiscal 1997 to $9.36 billion, were hurt by the company's program to eliminate trade promotion primarily in North America.
Domestic sales volumes fell 3.4 percent, while foreign sales volumes rose 1.9 percent.
Worldwide prices increased 1.7 percent and acquisitions, net of divestitures, contributed an additional 2.5 percent to sales. The effect of foreign exchange translation rates was negligible.
Including restructuring charges and gains on the sale of its New Zealand ice cream business and real estate in the United Kingdom, Heinz reported a loss of $0.61 for 1997.
The company said that in in September it will launch a new Weight Watchers 1-2-3 Success program which has been very successful in Europe.
Heinz also noted that its outsourcing production of a portion of its tomato paste requirements will reduce investment in a capital-intensive business.
